title: Injury, cut, burn or fall

fields.question: Is there heavy bleeding that will not stop with firm pressure?
fields.description: Is there heavy bleeding that will not stop with firm pressure?

fields.question: Was there a blow to the head?
fields.description: Was there a blow to the head?

fields.question: Any confusion, drowsiness or trouble staying awake?
fields.description: Any confusion, drowsiness or trouble staying awake?

fields.question: Is there an obvious deformity, or can the person not move it or put weight on it?
fields.description: Is there an obvious deformity, or can the person not move it or put weight on it?

fields.question: Is the wound deep, gaping, or does it show fat or muscle?
fields.description: Is the wound deep, gaping, or does it show fat or muscle?

fields.question: Is it a burn that is large, blistering, or on the face, hands or genitals?
fields.description: Is it a burn that is large, blistering, or on the face, hands or genitals?

fields.question: Any numbness, tingling or colour change beyond the injury?
fields.description: Any numbness, tingling or colour change beyond the injury?

rules.reason: A blow to the head should be assessed the same day.
Possible broken bone or serious joint injury.
Deep wounds may need closing or cleaning the same day.
Large burns or burns on sensitive areas need same-day care.
Numbness or colour change may mean nerve or blood-supply injury.
The person rates the injury as severe.
Signs of infection should be reviewed by a doctor.
The person rates the injury as moderate.

warning_signs: Confusion or repeated vomiting after a head injury
source_notes: Rules are student-authored from the general principles in public triage guidance (NHS emergency advice, ESI handbook, WHO emergency triage). Source clause references still to be added; NOT clinically validated.
